selectedOriginals.inspection: 2010 full west-front/north-end original: red lower brick, yellow exposed red timber upper floor, black sash windows, four-column semicircular balcony, main end gable, cross gable and spired attic.
2016 entrance detail resolves round steps, column pedestals/volutes, white balusters, branching timber patterns, coloured attic window, twin louvred spire dormers and copper tile courses.

sources.inspection: Official Cultural Affairs description: brick first floor and wood second, semicircular neoclassical entry balcony, steep roof and central spired cupola.
Official architecture account: Ionic columns, branching wooden beams, copper tiled roof and red/yellow/green garret glass.
Aerial inspected: main roof/ridges and entry projection; detached southern cafe and other park structures excluded.

scope: Historic Tudor-style house, entrance balcony/round steps, own roof turrets and small rear terrace. Detached park/cafe buildings and modern access enclosure excluded.
limits: Only the two selected original images used for facade details. Unseen rear openings and partly hidden roof joins remain conservative estimates. No photo pixels redistributed.

specificRoofAmbiguitySupplement.inspection: 2006 frontal original inspected specifically for curved roof form behind the spired attic. Confirms rounded gable/rooflet belonging to the house; hidden connection and full depth are estimated. Also confirms entrance balcony back opens to door, without a transverse railing.
